desc: Implement the `countSubstrings` method using the derived $O(N)$ algorithm with a helper array `cnt` of size 10 to track the number of substrings ending at the current position divisible by each digit 1-9.
Inside the loop over the string, for each position `i` and digit `d = s[i]`, compute the updated counts `new_cnt[k]` for all `k` in 1-9 by solving the modular equation `val * 10 % k == -d % k`.
Handle the case where `gcd(10, k) > 1` by summing the counts of valid residues modulo `k`.
Accumulate the result by adding `new_cnt[d]` to the total whenever `d` is non-zero.
Ensure the solution handles leading zeros correctly by treating the numeric value of substrings (which can have leading zeros) as standard integers in the modulo arithmetic.
Verify the implementation with the provided examples ("12936", "5701283", "1010101010") and edge cases like "0", "00", "10" are handled correctly.
